newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe civil servants vow to press on with strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe civil servants vow to press on with strike.

text.p: Striking Zimbabwean civil servants vowed on Friday to stay on the streets until the government awarded them higher allowances and negotiated their working conditions.

Thousands of the strikers, mainly junior doctors and nurses, milled about a park in central Harare on Friday morning, ignoring assurances from the government that it was talking to their representatives about their demands.

"We are going to carry on with the strike for as long as government takes to meet our demands. It's entirely up to the government to come up with a solution quickly then we will go back to work," Austin Bene, one of the strike leaders, told Reuters.
Some hospitals around the country have called in army medical personnel to help senior doctors handle emergencies.

This is the second time in two months that the civil servants have gone on strike. Last month, the government of President Robert Mugabe finally agreed to award them a 20 percent pay increase after they had stayed on the streets for three weeks, paralysing essential social services.

It also agreed to open negotiations by September 24 on their conditions of services and demands for higher allowances but later twice postponed the talks, angering the civil servants who decided to go on strike again to stop the delays.

Bene said about 12,000 junior doctors and nurses were on the streets around the country but a spokesman for the Public Service Association to which they are affiliated refused to be drawn into saying how many of its members were involved.
